newsitem.title: GERMANY: Springer sees clearly improved 97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Springer sees clearly improved 97 profit.

text.p: German media group Axel Springer Velag AG said on Thursday it expected lower paper costs, productivity gains and reduced losses in fledgling businesses to lead to "clearly improved" profit in 1997, after 1996 net profit rose 15.5 percent to 164 million marks ($97.2 million).
The company, which owns the mass circulation Bild newspaper and the Sat 1 cable television channel, said news print costs in 1996 rose about 100 million marks to 657 million marks.

Earlier on Thursday Springer said 1996 sales rose 4.3 percent to 4.426 billion marks. It planned to raise its dividend to 20 marks per share from 17 marks. -- Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.687 German Marks)
